keyVerseText: And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.
rootMeaning: The root word עֶכֶס (ʻekeç) refers to a fetter or a tinkling ornament such as an anklet or bangle, emphasizing a decorative yet binding object worn around the ankle. The feminine form עַכְסָה (ʻAkçâh) literally means "anklet," which conveys both the idea of adornment and a symbol of connection or belonging. This root meaning enriches the common English gloss of the name Achsah by highlighting the cultural and symbolic significance of the anklet as more than just a personal name, but as a marker of identity and relationship within the community.
usageInScripture: The word עַכְסָה appears five times in Scripture and is consistently translated as "Achsah," referring to a proper name of a woman, specifically the daughter of Caleb. The top translations show a uniformity in rendering it as a personal name rather than a common noun, indicating the importance of this individual in the biblical narrative. This consistency reflects the word’s primary function as a proper name, while its root meaning as an anklet subtly underscores her identity and heritage within the tribe of Israel.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עַכְסָה as both a name and an anklet enriches our appreciation of biblical names as carriers of meaning and covenantal identity. Achsah, as the daughter of Caleb, represents the fulfillment of God’s promises to His people, embodied in the land and relationships He grants. The anklet imagery can remind believers of how God adorns His people with blessings and binds them into His covenant family. This dual significance points to the personal and communal dimensions of faith, where God’s promises are both treasured and lived out in faithful obedience.
keyVerseReflection: In Joshua 15:16, Caleb promises his daughter Achsah as a wife to the one who captures Kirjathsepher, directly connecting her as a reward for faithfulness and courage. The use of the name Achsah here not only identifies a person but subtly evokes the root meaning of an anklet, symbolizing a treasured gift and a binding covenant relationship. This verse highlights how God’s blessings often come through faithful service and obedience, with Achsah representing the tangible fulfillment of God’s promise to His people.
